document_title: Seven ways to slow a data center

strings: Seven ways to slow a data center
Seven Texas governmental bodies acted this year. No two reached for the same instrument.
One each. The shape of the instrument decides whether anything stops.
The last three came inside 21 days of each other.
The council adopted a resolution that starts a process. The city's own release names no pause in force today.
The newest pause is not in force
CITY OF FORT WORTH, C22 AND C23
Five of the seven stop nothing
"does not stop the project from moving forward"
"Resolutions do nothing, they are not binding."
The Killeen commission's vote is a recommendation. The council decides.
Two of the seven have teeth
"Approved 7-0 at the June 16, 2026 City Council meeting."
BRAZORIA COUNTY, C9 THE ZONE THEY STOOD ON
SAN ANGELO, C12 CAPPED BY ORDINANCE
One refused the zone. One wrote the limit into the water ordinance.
Four applications. None was voted on.
Commissioner Linder made a motion to deny order 1.3.
THE RECORD CARRIES THE SAME MINUTE ON EACH OF THE FOUR
GRANTING TAX ABATEMENT OF OLD OCEAN DATACENTER LLC
No action taken due to I.3 failed
Tom Green County's court voted not to pursue a moratorium in Precinct 4.
A commissioner referenced a $100 million lawsuit filed against Hill County after it approved a similar one year moratorium.
TOM GREEN COUNTY, C15 AND C16 REPORTED SPEECH ABOUT A LAWSUIT
The water board denied a petition asking it to project data center water demand.
Ten bodies in this record took one up. Seven acted and three did not.
Fort Worth holds the first of two required public hearings.
THE CITY'S OWN WORDING IS A DEADLINE RATHER THAN A FIXED DATE
Fort Worth is the only one of the ten still carrying a dated step.
